https://calgary.citynews.ca/2026/07/19/w.text: What to know about the Tate brothers, social media influencers facing rape and trafficking charges FILE - Andrew Tate, left, watches his brother Tristan speak, outside a police station in Voluntari, Romania, May 21, 2025. (AP Photo/Vadim Ghirda, File) Copyright 2025 The Associated Press. All rights reserved. By Sylvia Hui, The Associated Press, Posted Jul 19, 2026 5:49 am. LONDON (AP) — Influencer brothers Andrew and Tristan Tate were arrested Saturday in Miami after U.K. prosecutors said they brought further rape and sex trafficking charges against them. Britain’s Crown Prosecution Service said the new charges relate to four further victims and were brought after authorities received evidence from Bedfordshire Police in southeastern England. The charges include rape, assault, trafficking and offences relating to “indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.” The charges announced Saturday, which bring the total number of alleged victims in the U.K. to seven, are the latest in a long-running international legal saga involving the brothers that has spanned the U.S., Britain and Romania. The brothers have denied wrongdoing. Here are some things to know about the Tate brothers: Who the Tate Brothers are Andrew Tate, 39, and Tristan Tate, 38, are dual U.S.-British citizens known for their social media empire promoting wealth, male dominance and misogyny. Andrew Tate is a former professional kickboxer and self-described misogynist who has amassed more than 10 million followers, most of them boys and young men, on X. He has been banned from platforms like YouTube, TikTok and Instagram for violating hate speech guidelines. He also runs an online academy where he says he teaches young men how to get rich and attract women. Tristan Tate is also a former kickboxer. The brothers are avid supporters of U.S. President Donald Trump. What the Tates are charged with Andrew Tate and his brother have faced multiple charges in the U.K. and Romania , where they moved to in 2016. British prosecutors said the new charges relate to alleged offenses that took place between 2010 and 2017. They said Andrew Tate was charged with seven further counts of rape, three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, three counts of assault and 19 charges for offenses relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography. Tristan Tate was charged with one count of sexual assault, two counts of rape and three counts of arranging or facilitating sex trafficking. The Crown Prosecution Service said in a statement it “has requested the extradition of the Tates from the U.S. They have been arrested and await extradition proceedings to the U.K.” The Tates already face previous charges of rape, bodily harm, human trafficking and controlling prostitution for gain relating to three other alleged victims in the U.K. between 2012 and 2015. In June, a U.K. High Court judge threw out a legal bid by the Tates to be told the names of their accusers. In Romania, the siblings were arrested in late 2022 along with two Romanian women. The four were accused of participating in criminal schemes to lure women for sexual exploitation. They denied those allegations and the Romanian case hasn’t gone forward because of legal and procedural problems. The case hasn’t been closed, and there is also a separate legal case against the brothers in Romania. Andrew Tate has repeatedly claimed that prosecutors in Romania have no evidence against him and that there is a political conspiracy to silence him. Why the Tates were in the U.S. British police previously sought the Tates’ extradition to the U.K. once their legal proceedings in Romania concluded. But in February 2025 they were allowed to leave Romania after authorities lifted travel restrictions, and they flew to Florida on a private jet. Romania’s foreign minister said at the time that a U.S. official in the Trump administration had expressed interest in the brothers’ legal case in Romania. Trump said he knew “nothing about” the case when asked if his administration pressured the Romania government to release the Tates. https://www.dw.com/en/kenya-helicopter-c.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5J7Gc Scenic helicopter flights over remote wilderness are popular in Kenya but accidents are increasing Image: Kenya Red Cross/Handout/REUTERS Advertisement Authorities in Kenya say that all seven people on board a safari helicopter — six passengers and a pilot — were killed on Wednesday when the chopper crashed in the foothills of the popular but remote tourist destination, Mount Ololokwe. Kenya's Civil Aviation Authority said the group's Eurocopter EC130 B4 helicopter crashed at 9:13 a.m. (0613 GMT) after departing the Loisaba wildlife reserve on route to the Ewaso Nyiro area in Samburu County north of the Kenyan capital, Nairobi, adding that an investigation is underway to determine the cause of the crash. Video footage on social media showed the smoking wreckage of the helicopter strewn about, smoldering and burning in thickly wooded terrain. The helicopter went down in thick brush making it difficult for rescue workers to access the site Image: Kenya Red Cross/Handout/REUTERS What do we know about the victims of the Kenya crash? The US State Department said that five of the six passengers killed were US citizens. "The US Embassy is in touch with local authorities and is providing consular assistance," read a statement. "We extend our deepest condolences to the families and loved ones on their loss." An executive at Telemundo — a US-based Spanish-language television channel owned by Comcast/NBCUniversal — was reportedly among the victims. Michele Sensi-Contugi, director of Ecuador 's Strategic Intelligence Center was as well, and so was his wife, who also held US citizenship. Sensi-Contugi, a former businessman, was a close friend and associate of Ecuador's right-wing President Daniel Noboa , who appointed him head of national intelligence in 2024. "In this moment of deep sorrow, the government extends its heartfelt condolences to his family, loved ones and close associates," Ecuador's presidency said in a statement on X. More accidents as tourism grows Numerous travel companies offer helicopter tours to remote places like Mount Ololokwe. But as Kenya's tourism sector has grown, so, too, has the frequency of helicopter crashes . In February, another chopper went down in the wilderness, killing all six on board, including a parliamentarian. https://www.trend.az/casia/kazakhstan/42.text: Home Central Asia Kazakhstan World’s largest asset managers BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, Capital Group and Brookfield gather in Astana (PHOTO) Kazakhstan News 9 September 2026 09:09 (UTC +04:00) Global Capital in Astana: AFD 2026 Brings Together Asset Managers with US $26 Trillion Under Management Astana Finance Days brings together representatives of the world’s leading financial institutions, including BlackRock, the world’s largest asset manager with more than US$15 trillion in assets under management, also Goldman Sachs, Capital Group, Brookfield, E Fund Management, Rothschild & Co., IFC Asset Management Company, Hong Kong Investment Corporation and other global financial organisations. The companies represented at the forum collectively manage over US$26 trillion in assets. On September 9 and 10, the Astana International Financial Centre is hosting the 9th financial forum, Astana Finance Days 2026: Delivering Impact. Capital in Action. It brings together investors, representatives of the financial and technology sectors, regulators, government and quasi-government institutions, and international businesses. The forum attracted 8000 participants from 90 countries . The forum’s programme focuses on capital markets and investment products, regulation and the legal environment, institutional-scale innovation, financing of the real sector of the economy, as well as regional and cross-border cooperation. “Today's competition for capital requires not only attractive terms but also the ability to transform opportunities into real projects and investments. This is the essence of Astana Finance Days 2026: Delivering Impact. Capital in Action. We bring together investors, regulators, and businesses to transform ideas into practical solutions, investment projects, and long-term partnerships,” noted Renat Bekturov, Governor of the AIFC . The first day’s business programme begins with sessions on the role of sovereign and institutional capital in economic growth, the future of financial infrastructure, the tokenisation of real-world assets, investor protection, sustainable finance and the development of real-sector projects. The day’s central event will be the plenary session, “Rewiring the Architecture of Finance”. Speakers will include Timur Suleimenov, Governor of the National Bank of Kazakhstan; Renat Bekturov, Governor of the AIFC; Timur Turlov, Chief Executive Officer of Freedom Holding Corp.; Balaji Srinivasan , founder of Network School and bestselling author of The Network State; and Sergio Mello , Global Head of Stablecoin Solutions at Anchorage Digital. The session will be moderated by Sallianne Taylor , Head of Government Relations for EMEA at Bloomberg. Participants will discuss how technology, regulation and new models of capital movement are reshaping financial markets. The global financial system is entering a new era in which digital assets are becoming an integral part of public policy, while artificial intelligence is beginning to manage capital flows. The digital tenge, crypto reserves, AI regulation and decentralised finance are no longer abstract concepts but part of national agendas and business strategies. How do national regulators, development institutions and global technology companies envision the future of the global financial system and the evolving map of capital flows? The session will bring together key architects of the emerging financial order to discuss the transformation of financial infrastructure and the future of digital assets. Ben Powell , Managing Director and Chief Investment Strategist for the Middle East and APAC — BlackRock Investment Institute, will offer a distinct perspective on the new capital markets cycle. During the session “Sovereign and Institutional Capital as Catalysts for Growth and Strategic Transformation,” participants will discuss how sovereign and institutional investors can support long-term development, structural transformation and the implementation of large-scale projects. The discussion will feature representatives of the Hong Kong Investment Corporation, Fitch Ratings and other financial institutions. The technology track will continue with the sessions “The Future of Financial Infrastructure” and “Capital Beyond Borders: Tokenisation and the New Financial Infrastructure.” Representatives of the Development Bank of Kazakhstan, the National Payment Corporation of Kazakhstan, Mastercard, Janus Henderson Investors, Bir Ecosystem, Phillip Securities, Solana, The Open Platform and Commodity Chain will discuss the development of payment infrastructure, digital assets and new mechanisms for capital movement. One of the key industry topics on the first day will be the financing of junior exploration companies and early-stage mining projects. The session “Financing Junior Mining Projects: Challenges and Opportunities” will feature representatives of Solidcore, Alphamar, Elistra Advisory and Aurora Minerals Group. The programme will continue with keynote presentations by representatives of KAZ Minerals, Solidcore Resources, AGS, Zubr Capital, Freedom Holding Corp. and BI Group , focusing on the technological transformation of the economy, investment in AI infrastructure and computing capacity, the development of innovation clusters, attracting international capital, and the commercial real estate market. The programme will also feature project pitches and investor matchmaking sessions with potential investors. In April this year, the AIFC launched the Junior Mining Platform to attract investment into early-stage exploration projects and opened applications for junior companies. The AIFC platform connects junior companies with domestic and international investors. Of the 48 projects submitted, 23 were selected and will be presented to investors during a pitching session at the forum. The forum will also feature the second annual meeting of the Turkic Green Finance Council , bringing together representatives of financial regulators, government bodies and development institutions from across the Turkic region. Participants will include Kubanychbek Omuraliev, Secretary General of the Organization of Turkic States; Baghdad Amreyev, President of the Turkic Investment Fund; and representatives of the Central Bank of Azerbaijan, the Kyrgyz Stock Exchange, the Hungarian National Bank, the AIFC Green Finance Centre and other organisations. Also on the first day, a closed meeting of the AIFC Islamic Finance Advisory Board will be held. Financial security will be addressed during the session “Financial Intelligence in the Digital Age: From Virtual Assets to Artificial Intelligence.” Representatives of the Egmont Group, Sherlocq, Eurasian Bank and the Astana Financial Services Authority will discuss how the development of digital technologies is changing approaches to identifying financial risks and interactions between the public and private sectors. A separate track will focus on the AIFC’s legal infrastructure. The session “Capital in Action: How the AIFC Court and IAC Protect Investor Rights” will feature Chief Justice of the AIFC Court, the Chairman of the International Arbitration Centre and other speakers. The session will examine how the AIFC Court and IAC protect investor rights through effective international dispute resolution and digital innovation. Participants will also discuss institutional dispute-resolution strategies aimed at increasing transparency, strengthening investor confidence and supporting sustainable investment in Kazakhstan. At the forum, the AIFC will also debut AIDA — the AIFC Intelligent Digital Assistant AIDA is a multilingual intelligent assistant designed to support clients and help them navigate the Centre’s services. It processes text and voice queries, provides information about AIFC registration, applicable requirements, procedures and services, and, where necessary, directs users to the appropriate department or specialist. Forum participants will be able to test the system in different languages in real time. The first day’s regional track will continue with the AFSA roundtable “From Fragmentation to Integration: Regional Cooperation to Strengthen Financial Markets.” It will bring together representatives of financial regulators from Georgia, the Kyrgyz Republic, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan, as well as international financial organisations and development institutions, including the Asian Development Bank, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the World Bank and the International Finance Corporation. Representatives of Bloomberg and stock exchanges from Central Asia and the South Caucasus will also participate. The roundtable will address key barriers to cross-border capital flows and practical measures to expand access to financial markets, facilitate mutual recognition and information exchange, and strengthen supervisory cooperation. During the day, several agreements are expected to be signed. These include a Memorandum of Understanding between the National Bank of Georgia and the Astana Financial Services Authority (AFSA) to facilitate access and recognition in the financial services sector, as well as a Memorandum of Understanding between AFSA and the Croatian Financial Services Supervisory Agency (HANFA) to strengthen regulatory cooperation and deepen the partnership. As part of the AIFC grain tokenisation initiative , Tech Hub Limited is also expected to sign separate Memoranda of Understanding with Concordia Group Ltd. and Aitas Agro Ltd. to advance technological solutions and develop new instruments for the agricultural market. An important component of the forum will be the AFD Exhibition Hub , an exhibition platform bringing together financial institutions, banks, investment and asset management companies, and fintech and technology projects. Participants will present their products, solutions and achievements while establishing direct contacts with potential partners and investors. Astana Finance Days 2026 is being held with the support of its partners. Freedom is the forum’s Gold Partner; Solidcore Resources, KAZ Minerals and ITS are Silver Partners; LMAX Group and Teniz Capital Investment Banking are Bronze Partners; Allur is the Industry Partner; Binance is the Crypto Partner; Mastercard is the Fintech Partner; Air Astana is the Official Airline; Euronews and SCMP as the International Media Partners. Other partners include Orient Capital Management, Dana Capital Limited, BI Group, CICC, Roemer Capital (Europe), Masdar, E Fund Management (Hong Kong), Abylai Global Solutions, Symphony Digital Assets, Fitch Ratings, AmCham Kazakhstan, Solana, Halyk Finance, MYD Production, Atlas Capital, PwC, Anchorage Digital, Alif, Jupiter Jet, RCS Group, Zubr Capital, Vitis Capital, Amicorp, Code Coin and others. Παραμένουν οι πιέσεις από πετρέλαιο και ομόλογα - Ο S&P +0,2% Άμυνα – Διπλωματία Παρασκευή 11/09/2026 - 17:56 Greece supplied 340,000 weapons worth up to 450M euros to Ukraine Greece Ukraine War in Ukraine Militarnyi BMP1A1 Ost Mitsotakis administration missiles artillery tags : Over 340,000 pieces of military hardware, including 40 BMP-1s, approximately 190 artillery pieces, hundreds of thousands of shells and rocket systems, allocated by the Mitsotakis administration to Ukraine A bombshell was dropped by Ukrainian media, revealing that over 340,000 pieces of military hardware, including 40 BMP-1 vehicles, approximately 190 artillery guns, hundreds of thousands of artillery shells and rocket systems, as well as Crotale missiles, have been transferred to Ukraine by the government of Kyriakos Mitsotakis since the eruption of the war in February 2022 , according to an analysis published by the Ukrainian defense portal Militarnyi on September 10 . The valuation of total Greek military assistance, which encompasses transfers executed via intermediary states, ranges, according to the same analysis, between 350 and 450 million euros. It appears that the obsessive alignment of the Mitsotakis government with the NATO doctrine of the «right side of history» not only damages historic ties with Moscow , but has also proven extraordinarily costly for the wallets of Greek taxpayers. The question remains: who will answer, and in what manner, for this continuous diplomatic and geostrategic transgression that initiated in 2022 and endures to this day... 4 years of subordination to NATO strategy, 4 years backing the Zelensky regime Greek military assistance toward Ukraine , over the span of four years, evolved from the urgent dispatch of small arms and ammunition drawn from active arsenals of the Hellenic Armed Forces into the provision of armored fighting vehicles, artillery platforms, air defense systems, training modules for Ukrainian military personnel, and the emergence of bilateral defense-industrial cooperation. From the opening days of the conflict, Athens dispatched weaponry to Ukraine , while in autumn 2022 deliveries of BMP-1 infantry fighting vehicles commenced under a circular exchange agreement (Ringtausch) with Germany for their replacement with German Marder infantry fighting vehicles. In subsequent years, artillery pieces and munitions played a pivotal role in military support, part of which was channeled through multilateral frameworks involving the United States , Germany , and the Czech Republic . According to the Ukraine Support Tracker of the Kiel Institute for the World Economy , between January 24, 2022 and June 30, 2026 , Greece committed 169 million euros directly in bilateral aid to Ukraine , a figure corresponding to 0.093% of Greek GDP. The initiation of military aid The decision to supply armaments to Ukraine was adopted by the administration of Kyriakos Mitsotakis during the opening days of the conflict in February 2022 . On February 27, 2022 , Greece announced the shipment of military materiel aboard two C-130 transport aircraft. This move represented an unconventional departure for Athens . Prior to 2022 , Greece abstained from providing weapons to active belligerents in armed hostilities. Consequently, the resolution to furnish direct military support to Ukraine marked a notable pivot from established national policy. The inaugural shipment comprised largely Soviet-legacy weapons systems held in Greek depots that could be absorbed by the Ukrainian military without extensive operational retraining. According to tracking by Oryx , since February 2022 Greece transferred to Ukraine 20,000 Kalashnikov assault rifles, 815 RPG-18 disposable anti-tank rocket launchers, and an unquantified inventory of 122mm artillery rockets. Russian Kalashnikovs... from Greece to Ukraine Concurrently, small arms ammunition consignments were completed. A portion of this weaponry bore a distinctive background: the Kalashnikov rifles originated from contraband shipments previously confiscated by Greek maritime and border authorities. The composition of the initial aid reflected a pragmatic formula: transferring materiel that was immediately available and matched the logistical standards of the Ukrainian armed forces. The transfer of armored platforms proved more intricate. Greece maintained a significant inventory of BMP-1A1 Ost infantry fighting vehicles, former East German military stocks absorbed by the Bundeswehr following German reunification and subsequently transferred to Greece in the 1990s. In total, Athens had acquired roughly 500 such BMPs , though elements were later transferred to Iraq and Egypt . For Ukraine , these vehicles presented high utility due to familiar design parameters and rapid operational integration. Athens , however, declined to release the BMPs without securing prior backfill replacements. The deadlock was resolved via the German Ringtausch swap initiative, whereby nations delivered Soviet-standard materiel to Ukraine in return for modern Western armor from Germany . The BMP-1 transfer and the «triangular» deal with Germany In late May 2022 , then-German Chancellor Olaf Scholz unveiled an accord whereby Greece would transfer BMP-1 vehicles to Ukraine , while Germany would supply Marder infantry fighting vehicles as replacements. Initially, the precise scope of the transfer remained ambiguous. In June , Kyriakos Mitsotakis cited a figure of 20 to 30 BMP-1s , although Greek defense sources had previously floated significantly higher numbers. The definitive parameters were finalized in September . Greece would deliver 40 BMP-1A1 units to Ukraine , receiving in exchange 40 Marder 1A3 vehicles from Germany . The operational blueprint stipulated synchronized deliveries: the Greek side would release its inventory as German counterparts arrived on Greek soil. Sealing the Ukrainian alignment and visits to Kyiv The first Marder units touched down in Greece on October 17, 2022 , and on October 19 Ukrainian Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba announced that shipments of Greek BMP-1s had commenced. According to Oryx , all 40 vehicles are cataloged within verified Greek deliveries to Ukraine . The Greek BMP-1s incorporated modifications compared to original Soviet baselines. Following acquisition from East German depots, they had been modernized to Western standards and designated BMP-1A1 Ost . Across select vehicles in Greek service, primary armaments were supplemented or replaced with heavy .50 caliber M2 Browning machine guns, while other BMP-1s were modified to mount twin 23mm ZU-23-2 anti-aircraft cannons. The armor transfers unfolded alongside intensified political engagements between Athens and Kyiv . In October 2022 , the President of the Hellenic Republic, Katerina Sakellaropoulou , accompanied by Minister of National Defense Nikos Panagiotopoulos , visited Ukraine . By that juncture, the BMP-1 transfer had transitioned from diplomatic deliberations to operational realization, anchoring military assistance as a structural pillar of bilateral ties between Greece and Ukraine . Artillery and ammunition Following the 2022 initial transfers, ammunition became a primary axis of Greek military support to Ukraine . Greek arsenals held substantial stockpiles of artillery shells across varied calibers, particularly for weapon systems that, according to Ukrainian accounts, were losing operational centrality within the Hellenic Armed Forces , yet remained indispensable for the Ukrainian battlefield. Unlike the BMP-1 swap, a significant portion of these deliveries was executed indirectly via intermediary partners, chiefly the United States and the Czech Republic . In November 2023 , it emerged that discussions were underway between Athens and Washington regarding the sale of 75,000 artillery shells from Greek stockpiles to the US , with Ukraine as the final end-user. The arrangement encompassed 50,000 rounds of 105mm, 20,000 rounds of 155mm, and 5,000 rounds of 203mm artillery shells, valued at approximately $47 million. The 203mm heavy shells were of notable operational importance, a caliber largely phased out across most NATO members, but critically needed for Ukrainian 2S7 Pion self-propelled guns and Western-supplied M110 howitzers. In 2024 , the Czech Republic emerged as the central conduit for channeling Greek ammunition to Ukraine under the Czech ammunition initiative. In March , the newspaper Kathimerini reported that a deal was being structured under which Prague would procure Greek defense materiel for onward transfer to Ukraine . The inventory submitted by Athens was extensive: 2,000 5-inch Zuni aircraft rockets, 180 2.75-inch rockets, 90,000 90mm rounds, and 4 million rounds of small arms ammunition. The valuation of this materiel package sold to the Czech Republic was estimated at approximately 150 million euros. Heavy tube artillery was integrated within the same framework. Greece made available 70 towed 155mm M114A1 howitzers, categorized as non-essential for the operational requirements of the Greek military. Transfer of M114 and M110 howitzers via the Czech channel The M114 is an American artillery system dating to World War II, yet its standard 155mm caliber made it immediately usable by Ukraine , which faced acute artillery deficits. According to Greek defense reporting, this constituted the second tranche of howitzers designated for sale to the Czech Republic and subsequent delivery to the Ukrainian military. An even larger arrangement centered on 203mm heavy artillery. In September 2025 , Greek press reports indicated that the sale of 60 M110A2 self-propelled howitzers to the Czech Republic was being prepared. Accompanying the guns was a massive ordnance cache: 50,000 M106 high-explosive shells, 40,000 M650 HERA rocket-assisted projectiles, 30,000 M404 ICM cluster munitions, and 30,000 M509A1 DPICM rounds. In aggregate, the inventory totaled 150,000 rounds of 203mm ammunition. The baseline valuation of the M110A2 howitzers alone was estimated at €31.2 million, while the comprehensive arms and munitions package was valued at approximately €199.4 million. This hardware stemmed primarily from inventories designated as surplus to operational doctrine. For Athens , the transaction freed depot capacity and provided revenue earmarked for defense modernization programs. For Ukraine , 203mm ammunition represented irreplaceable battlefield stock: industrial production across NATO had ceased, yet Ukrainian artillery brigades continued to operate systems reliant on this heavy caliber. Initial press reports did not provide definitive proof that the equipment had departed Greece. Clarity was provided by official submissions made by Athens to the United Nations Register of Conventional Arms ( UNROCA ) for 2025 . Greek howitzers on the UN registry Greece officially declared the export to the Czech Republic of 66 M110A2 203mm self-propelled howitzers, 68 M114 155mm towed howitzers, and 56 M101 105mm towed howitzers. Thus, the verified scope of artillery transfers exceeded earlier proposals that focused strictly on the M110A2 and M114 platforms. However, UNROCA documentation lists the Czech Republic as the recipient state rather than Ukraine . While bilateral agreements make it plausible that this materiel was slated for Ukraine , independent operational verification is required before confirming that all 66 M110A2s , 68 M114s , and 56 M101s are in active service with Ukrainian forces. The reliance on the Czech conduit and third-party mechanisms explains why public estimates of total Greek military contributions to Ukraine display broad variations. Air defense systems Air defense proved the most complex chapter in defense cooperation between Athens and Kyiv . Ukraine repeatedly appealed to Greece due to its diversified anti-aircraft inventory, encompassing Soviet and Russian systems alongside American Patriot batteries. However, Greek force posture was directly tied to sovereign territorial air defense obligations. Negotiations regarding distinct systems followed divergent paths. The Greek S-300PMU-1 long-range system generated the highest international attention. Originally purchased by Cyprus , the systems were redeployed to Crete following the missile crisis of the late 1990s and later transferred to Greek ownership. Following the 2022 invasion, transferring them to Ukraine was repeatedly debated. In September 2022 , Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis stated publicly that Athens did not intend to dispatch the S-300 to Ukraine , underscoring that assistance would not come at the expense of national defense readiness. Over time, this stance adapted slightly, but the core prerequisite remained rigid: the S-300 could only depart if a modern Western equivalent was deployed in its place. Between S-300 and Patriot Greek media floated additional Patriot batteries as a candidate replacement. However, practical execution stalled, and the S-300PMU-1 remained within the order of battle of the Hellenic Air Force . A different operational policy applied to systems nearing obsolescence. In late December 2024 , the transfer of 24 RIM-7 Sea Sparrow surface-to-air missiles from Hellenic Navy and Air Force stocks to Ukraine was approved. These missiles were approximately forty years old and no longer matched national requirements. They held immediate battlefield value for Ukraine , whose forces adapted Soviet-era Buk missile systems to fire Western Sea Sparrow interceptors under the FrankenSAM program. Supplying Kyiv with Crotale missiles Greek assistance also encompassed interceptor missiles for French-manufactured Crotale short-range air defense systems. In April 2026 , Kathimerini reported that Greece had transferred Crotale missiles and related air defense ordnance to Ukraine . The precise quantity of these missiles has not been officially declassified. In 2026 , negotiations shifted toward the potential supply of Patriot interceptors. According to Kathimerini , Ukraine requested up to 200 PAC-2 missiles from Greece , items that had served within the Hellenic Air Force for roughly 23 years. Pressure regarding Patriot systems Allied capitals had previously evaluated transferring one of Greece's six operational Patriot batteries to Ukraine , an option rejected by Athens . The 2026 proposal bypassed launcher transfers, focusing strictly on missile stocks via an intermediary: Greece could sell PAC-2 missiles to Norway for subsequent donation to Ukraine . By September 2026 , Athens had not authorized either the transfer of Patriot batteries or the export of the requested interceptors, citing the necessity of preserving national air defense posture. Concurrently, Greece was negotiating the repatriation of the Patriot battery deployed to Saudi Arabia since 2021 . However, its recall did not imply the transfer of the system to Ukraine . https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/10/russ.text: Russia's designation of "unfriendly countries" has expanded beyond foreign economic policy into domestic courts, family law, property rights and financial obligations, with a string of decrees and rulings extending its reach to individuals.The list of states Moscow considers unfriendly was formalised as a form of retaliation in a government order in March 2022, weeks after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.It covers the US, the UK, Canada, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland, Ukraine, Australia, New Zealand and EU member states, all of which have pushed back against Russia's war of aggression.This autumn, the Russian government nearly doubled import duties on spirits from unfriendly countries, raising the rate from 20% to 35%, primarily affecting European and North American producers.Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the placement of foreign companies' Russian assets under temporary administration was directly linked to those companies' home countries being on the list.The measure has affected the Russian operations of Nestlé, Auchan, FM Logistic, Leroy Merlin, Metro Cash & Carry, Tarkett, Japan Tobacco International (JTI) and others.Russia's Supreme Court cited the unfriendly countries designation in a child custody dispute, ruling that returning a child to France could run counter to her interests in part because France appears on the list.In March 2025, Russian citizen Alexei Ermakov took his daughter on a two-week holiday to Turkey and Slovakia with the consent of her mother, Ukrainian citizen Anna Tishkova, then brought the child to Russia in April.He subsequently arranged Russian citizenship for the girl. Despite international agreements on returning children to their country of habitual residence, the court declined to order her return to France.Property and vehicles under threatA bill supported in the State Duma would allow vehicles stolen or illegally exported from unfriendly countries to be registered in Russia.Supporters say it addresses legal gaps caused by the breakdown in cooperation with Western states; opponents say it would weaken property protections for owners in those countries.In a separate case, the Supreme Court ordered the Interior Ministry to register a vehicle flagged in an international database at Canada's request, ruling that listing in an international stolen vehicles register is not in itself sufficient grounds to refuse registration in Russia.Putin signed a decree this autumn under which individuals who cannot prove citizenship of Russia or a friendly state or produce a residency permit are automatically treated as persons from unfriendly countries.A further decree allows Russian debtors to withhold payment from creditors in unfriendly countries, departing from the standard principle of equal treatment of parties to contracts.Standard principles of private international law require courts to resolve contracts, custody matters and property disputes on their legal merits, regardless of the nationality or political status of the parties.Russia’s application of a foreign-policy designation to those areas departs from norms in conventions it has ratified, among them the 1980 Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction, which obligates signatory states to return children removed across borders without consent.
